why: XLV +2.79 pct to $170.81: the $164.50-165.00 September floor held a second time Thursday (low $165.19 on 11.1M, the week's heaviest volume) and the fund reclaimed its stacked 20D/50D ($168.5); thirteen of fourteen names that fell last week rose; XLV regained its 50-day, taking the board's count to four of twelve (wiki/healthcare.md; wiki/synthesis.md Section 2).

The regime fit is low-beta and policy-driven: correlation to SPY 0.231, beta 0.52, and the Federal Register was quiet -- 'the damage was the news and not the numbers'; DXY crossed the 102 line and nothing happened (wiki/healthcare.md Ophelia; wiki/canary-watch.md SECTOR CORRELATION MATRIX).

Week RF raised 42 -> 50 and MC 40 -> 45: JNJ (10.4 pct of the fund) and UNH (5.4 pct) open earnings season Tuesday before the open with XLV 1.1 pts under its failed-breakout high $171.87; a clean morning puts $176.60 in play (wiki/healthcare.md; wiki/earnings-surveillance.md).

Data quality: BLFS is missing from the panel (9 of 10 constituents, status warn); the arithmetic is computed on nine names and risk_penalty is left at 0.0, consistent with the AVB-missing cycles in August-September (inputs/2026-10-09/healthcare.json data_quality).
risks: UNH's whisper ($4.60 vs $4.15 consensus) makes an in-line print a miss in the room; four of its last eight reaction days were -6 pct or worse; JNJ's +15.8 pct whisper gap is unconfirmed on a stock that moves 1.7 pct (wiki/earnings-surveillance.md CONSENSUS VS WHISPER).

A rally nobody can explain: no sourced cause for ELV +6.8, ISRG +8.2, ABBV +5.2 pct; Friday's +1.6 pct came on 7.0M shares, below average; the GLOBE-exposed biologics (REGN, MRK, VRTX) recovered least (wiki/healthcare.md WILD CARD).
Falsifier: a close under $165.00 -> 200D $155.91; managed-care prints confessing the cost trend (ISM services prices at their highest since 2022) reverse ELV/CI (wiki/healthcare.md RISK SCENARIOS).

why: Month arithmetic is the second-best on the board (relative momentum 90, +2.25 pts vs SPY, up-volume 79.4 pct) on a sector that fell hardest on the Sep 30 GLOBE final rule and paid it back in a week with no new policy action (wiki/healthcare.md; inputs/2026-10-09/healthcare.json metrics).

Cecil's list survived the rally: UNH 16.8x with a 26.7 pct gap, REGN 12.1x, ABT 16.4x, PFE at 6.1 pct; big pharma neutral, biologics neutral-negative until the calls size GLOBE (wiki/healthcare.md; wiki/synthesis.md Section 1).

Month RF raised 45 -> 50, MC held at 50: ISRG Oct 20, TMO/ABT/ELV Oct 21, LLY Oct 29 (15.1 pct of the fund), MRK/BMY/GILD Oct 29, ABBV/REGN Oct 30, PFE/AMGN Nov 3, CVS Nov 4 -- the GLOBE commentary arrives on these calls (wiki/healthcare.md EARNINGS CALENDAR).
risks: GLOBE's precedent is final-rule Medicare policy (April 2027 start, ~5 pct of proposed scale); a larger scale or added category, or harsh Nov 30 negotiated prices, re-opens the sell-off (wiki/healthcare.md MACRO OVERLAY).

DXY above 102 lands on LLY, MRK, ABBV, JNJ translation Oct 13-30; concentration LLY ~15.1 pct + JNJ ~10.4 pct is a quarter of the fund; AMGN 4.7 pct over target on an unresolved binary (wiki/healthcare.md).
Small-cap biotech did not join: XBI -0.4 pct, under its 50D for a sixth week (wiki/healthcare.md SMALL/MID-CAP WATCH).

extracts.lead_summary: The floor held on the second visit and the sector took back everything it lost to the pricing rules. XLV rose 2.8% to $170.81 — the week's low of $165.19 came Thursday, a few cents above the $164.50–$165.00 September floor — and closed back over its 20-day and 50-day, which sit together at $168.5. Thirteen of the fourteen names that all fell last week rose this week (BMY was the exception). Managed care and medtech led (ELV +6.8%, ISRG +8.2%, CI +4.4%), AbbVie closed at a record ($276.47, +5.2%), Lilly reclaimed its 50-day, and J&J and UnitedHealth open earnings season Tuesday. I found no healthcare headline that explains the week; the policy news I carry from last week did not change, and the rally came without a sourced catalyst.
